statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path this score measures. Stress is 57 in the elevated band on a Saudi East-West pipeline still shut with no restart date, WTI marked $100.05, Houthi control of the Bab al-Mandeb approach and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 87 percent for an increase. Confidence is 85 on a complete evidence set re-verified against primary sources this hour.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Two independent facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, yet finished about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, while NQ futures traded down to 29,040.50 after the inflation print and recovered to settle 29,391.75, a round trip that retraced in both directions. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, fourteen hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one. Stress remains elevated and is described here as an environment reading only: under the fixed repository mapping it does not alter the mapped state.
headline: A fourth hour of a shut weekend tape leaves the Nasdaq-100 at its 29,368.44 close, VIX at 15.84 and WTI at $100.05, with no verified development since the last assessment: the Saudi East-West pipeline remains shut with no restart date and Houthi control of the Bab al-Mandeb approach is unchanged into a policy-decision week.
body:
This hour re-verified the full evidence set against primary sources and found no change. The Nasdaq-100 quote page still shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. NQ futures were wider and more instructive: a 29,040.50 low after the 12:30 UTC inflation print gave way to a 29,499.50 high and a 29,391.75 settle, a round trip in which mean reversion worked in both directions. The broader tape agreed, with the Dow up 0.98% to 52,573.29, the S&P 500 up 0.86% to 7,656.98 and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.96% to 26,333.04, each snapping a losing streak while still finishing the week lower. VIX remains 15.84, down 11.21%, having closed near the low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range.

The macro set behind that path is hawkish rather than disorderly. August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, both in line, with core at 0.3% on the month, one tenth above consensus. Friday's live coverage reported the implied probability of a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September meeting moving from about 70% during the morning to roughly 87% by the close. Treasury yields are firm, with the H.15 series re-checked this hour still showing the 10 September observation: the 2-year at 4.56%, the 5-year at 4.75%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37%. A firm but broadly in-line print that still allowed a 459-point round trip is evidence of orderly price discovery, which is why the event continues to raise Stress and not Tail.

The geopolitical set is unchanged and remains the reason Stress sits in the elevated band. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was shut Friday as a precaution after drone attacks and the latest verified reporting still gives no restart date. Verified analysis places Houthi forces in control of Yemen's Red Sea coastline and the Bab al-Mandeb approach, through which roughly 12% of global trade transits, while a reported Houthi statement declares navigation safe for all companies except Saudi vessels. Crude eased into the weekend rather than extending, with WTI settling near $100.05 after a 2.37% decline and Brent at $104.61, following reporting that Iran would meet Gulf states in Oman on safe commercial routes through the Strait of Hormuz. That combination, an unresolved supply outage against a credible de-escalation checkpoint, keeps the exposure in Stress and in conditional reopen-gap risk rather than in the observed price path that Tail measures.

The shared cross-asset context file was read at the start of this run. Its collection timestamp is more than ninety minutes old and its status is partial, so it is treated as stale supporting context and was not used as evidence of any current structure; the independent primary-source research above stands on its own. No danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one, and all twenty-four forecast slots lie inside the closure.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 09:00 UTC on 11 September to 08:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens in a trend-up read through the European hours, with Tail between 14 and 15 as the advance extended. The 12:30 UTC inflation print produced the only elevated readings of the window, Tail 21 and 22 in event/whipsaw mode with Confidence cut to 70 and then 80 while the post-release path was still forming. Tail fell back to 15 within ninety minutes as NQ retraced, held between 15 and 17 through the U.S. afternoon in mixed mode, then fell to 13 and 7 around the 21:00 UTC halt. The final nine slots sit at Tail 5 in normal mode, tracking the closure rather than a directional view, while Stress decayed steadily from 82 to 57 as the event passed and volatility fell.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, fourteen hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then steps to 7, 8 and 9 at roughly four-hour intervals before capping at 10 for the final eight slots as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of an eventual reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout. Stress runs 57 to a 61 ceiling and describes the environment rather than a path: a Saudi East-West pipeline outage with no restart date, WTI marked $100.05 after a 2.37% Friday decline, Houthi control of the Bab al-Mandeb approach qualified by a reported exemption for all non-Saudi vessels, a reported Iran-Gulf meeting in Oman on Hormuz shipping and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 87 percent for an increase. Confidence decays from 85 to a 78 floor as the verified evidence set ages without any live price path to refresh it. No danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one.
